pk.context: 200 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

clues.kinetics: Absolute bioavailability is 98%, with negligible first-pass metabolism, and food has no effect. About 55% is bound to plasma proteins, and it is cleared mainly by glucuronic acid conjugation.
clues.substance: Molecular weight 256.09. Very slightly soluble in water, 0.17 mg/mL at 25°C, with a pKa of 5.7.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA as scored tablets of 25, 100, 150 and 200 mg, and also as tablets for oral suspension and orally disintegrating tablets.
clues.safety: Boxed warning for serious skin rashes, including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, that can need hospitalization. Contraindicated in hypersensitivity; nausea, insomnia and somnolence are common.
clues.indication: Epilepsy: adjunctive therapy for partial-onset, generalized tonic-clonic and Lennox-Gastaut seizures from age 2, and conversion to monotherapy from age 16.
clues.mechanism: Its precise mechanism is unknown. A phenyltriazine chemically unrelated to other antiepileptics, it prevented seizure spread in maximal electroshock tests in animals.

tell: A phenyltriazine antiepileptic whose half-life runs from about 13 to 70 hours depending on co-medication, with a boxed rash warning.
